correctness.rationale: From the quartic equation, t=y+x^6/y and u=y-x^6/y satisfy the stated identities, and y=(t+u)/2. The simple zeros in the four cubic blocks show by valuation parity that the three quadratic classes CD, AB, AC are independent, also geometrically. The degree-eight cover is tamely ramified with index two at each of twelve finite roots, and unramified at infinity (even degrees), so Riemann–Hurwitz gives genus 17. The seven pullback spaces have distinct sign characters; within a space the displayed powers of x+1 are independent. Their dimensions 2,2,2,5,2,2,2 show that they exhaust canonical differentials. At x=-1 the four characters containing a simple zero in their squared representative contribute even vanishing orders: dx/u has order zero there. The other three contribute odd orders: dx/t has order one. Each ratio after removing common factors is a unit; square-root signs and constant normalization only scale individual rows. The independently recomputed even and odd jet matrices have full row ranks 11 and 6 with pivot columns [0,1,2,3,4,6,7,8,9,12,13] and [0,1,2,3,6,7], respectively, and pivot-minor determinants 1 and 4. Left-to-right pivots give the full filtration, and the two parities cannot cancel. Thus orders 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,12,13,14,15,16,18,24,26 give the displayed gaps upon adding one. The generators agree with the complement below 28, including the necessary indecomposable 18 and 26; the ten consecutive integers 28 through 37 all lie in the generated monoid, so addition of 10 covers the rest. The subgroup transitivity used is Lemma 4.4 of the defining paper, independent of its later Lemma 4.7. Lemma 4.7's prose reverses the condition on equality at 18P, but Appendix A explicitly tests dimension 5 at x(P)^12=1 and 4 otherwise and says the checks returned true. The frozen dimension 5 on the branch orbit is confirmed by the independently reconstructed gaps and is consistent with the appendix; it does not rely on the prose of Lemma 4.7.
